digest.component_or_area: Anthropic/Bedrock model settings and cache configuration
propositions: On agentic execution mode, tool-result message history is re-sent uncached every turn, causing input token cost to grow O(N^2) in the number of turns

Rebar telemetry cannot detect this inefficiency because warn_if_cache_ineffective only fires when cache_read_tokens is zero, but the system breakpoint masks the problem by registering non-zero cache hits

The pydantic-ai dependency exposes unused cache control keys (anthropic_cache and anthropic_cache_messages for Anthropic; bedrock_cache_messages for Bedrock) that are documented as the recommended multi-turn shape but remain unset in cache_settings_for
Bedrock and Anthropic require different cache control keys; using a shared top-level cache_control on Bedrock causes rejection, making per-provider configuration mandatory
Single-turn execution paths must remain byte-identical to avoid regression, requiring conditional logic gated on execution_mode
